why: A is the conjunction of the 16 theorems among the 22 declarations (universes 0). B is Theorem 6.41 plus the non-generic sentence. Hypotheses: A's give B's, since IsSectionOrientation → D640 is proved (D640_of_isSectionOrientation, rt_check OK). B's do not give A's. D640 → IsSectionOrientation needs a basis of sc-smoothly contractible neighbourhoods (see V6_60), and B's f lacks the tame germ data A uses at every smooth point. Corners: SolutionSetInGeneralPosition gives IsCompactCornerManifold by glue (proved), so with tame germ data A gives that part of B (corner_of_A). Orientation: A's continuity is path-wise, in the chart of an orientable pair; B asks for continuous local frames of ker f' on W ∩ S, in some chart, with the right ray. Either way needs real work: kernel continuity over S, local frames, sc-smooth paths of zeros, and tangentOr agreeing across charts (not formalized). B's part (2), orienting S_{f+s} through an induced orientation of f + s, is absent from the project. B ⇒ A also fails: B gives none of the lemmas and less than SolutionSetInGeneralPosition.
B_issue: Not a misreading: B follows the text's sc-smoothly contractible orientable neighbourhoods. But its hypothesis D640 constrains o only on such sets. Where none exist near a zero, D640 holds for arbitrary o, and B's conclusion TangentOrContinuous could fail. The blind author flags this, and it is not decided here. B reads the non-generic case for every sc⁺-perturbation s with f + s proper and generic, dropping 'small, supported near the zero set'. That looks harmless, since the induced orientation should exist for any s.
